title: WF03 F8 batch1 tenants edit page: missing GET /api/v1/tenants/:slug route caused Failed to load tenant; supervised integration symptom was not an actual post-cleanup stall
summary: Diagnosed the TM tenants blocker as a backend routing gap. The frontend edit page calls GET /api/v1/tenants/:slug, but the API router only exposed tenant list and tenant patch handlers. That made EditTenantPage fall into its Failed to load tenant branch. The separate integration symptom in the supervised log was also narrowed: the captured artifact shows the command exited with build exit code 58 after DB cleanup rather than hanging indefinitely at cleanup.

root_cause.details: src/main.zig wired GET /api/v1/tenants and PATCH /api/v1/tenants/:slug but never dispatched GET /api/v1/tenants/:slug. The service layer also had no getTenantAdmin helper, and src/api/routes/identity.zig had no tenant-detail handler. As a result, the edit-page fetch path could not succeed and the page rendered Failed to load tenant.

resolution.summary: Added the missing tenant detail service method, route handler, and main router dispatch so the edit page can load tenant data by slug.
verification: zig build exited 0 after the route fix.
Live API check with a real Keycloak admin token returned 200 for GET /api/v1/tenants/:slug after listing a tenant slug.
The exact integration command was rerun and advanced beyond 'Test database cleaned.' into integration test execution, disproving the original cleanup-stall interpretation.

occurrences.context: TM-UI-04/TM-UI-05 stopped on EditTenantPage with the last observed UI state 'Failed to load tenant.'
Diagnosis confirmed the edit page depended on a backend tenant detail route that was never exposed by the API router.

prevention: When adding a frontend detail page, verify the full CRUD surface is wired in the main API router, not just service and patch/list handlers.
Treat supervised integration 'stalls' as unverified until the captured log is checked for an actual process exit code or failing build step.
